claims.title: Customer order details may be observable before reaching the mobile app
claims.description: `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` carries browsing activity and order details containing PII, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If this customer-to-app path uses an unprotected transport, an attacker able to observe that path can intercept the customer's order details before `process:mobile-app` receives them. This is conditional on the unstated transport protection; the disclosed order context can then be correlated with the customer's subsequent API activity.

quotes.text: Customers browse and order through our mobile app

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` has unstated transport protection and the attacker must obtain an on-path position; impact is medium because the flow carries customer order details and `process:mobile-app` is tagged `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce protected customer-to-app transport
mitigations.detail: Establish how `flow:entity:customer>process:mobile-app>browse-and-order` is implemented and require authenticated encryption for any network leg carrying browsing or order details.

claims.title: Customer details are readable on the plaintext mobile-app API connection
claims.description: An attacker on the path of boundary-crossing `flow:process:mobile-app>process:web-api>api-traffic` can intercept customer details because the flow uses HTTP and has `encryption_in_transit: none`. The path carries order-placement traffic into internet-facing `process:web-api`; captured names, addresses, and order context can be used to target the customer records subsequently handled by `process:web-api` and `store:user-database`.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the flow crosses from `boundary:customer-device` to `boundary:sokify-internal-systems` with encryption stated absent, though the attacker still needs path access; impact is medium because the flow carries customer PII and order details.

mitigations.summary: Replace HTTP with TLS-protected API traffic
mitigations.detail: Require HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ for `flow:process:mobile-app>process:web-api>api-traffic`, and reject plaintext HTTP so customer details cannot be passively read in transit.

mitigations.summary: Minimize order data on the client-facing flow
mitigations.detail: Use opaque order references where possible and avoid sending fields not required by the mobile app.

claims.title: Catalogue-management SQL may be readable across the marketing boundary
claims.description: `flow:process:catalogue-spreadsheet>process:web-api>sql-statements` crosses from `boundary:marketing-office` to `boundary:sokify-internal-systems`, while its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport protection is absent, an observer on that path can intercept SQL statements revealing unpublished price and product-copy changes before they reach `process:web-api`. The disclosed statements expose the API's catalogue-management interface and can inform later attacks against that process.

quotes.text: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the crossing flow's transport protection is unstated and an attacker needs access to the marketing-to-internal path; impact is low because the stated payload is catalogue SQL affecting prices and product copy rather than customer records.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the spreadsheet-to-API channel
mitigations.detail: Use TLS with a distinct client identity for `flow:process:catalogue-spreadsheet>process:web-api>sql-statements` rather than an unstated transport.

mitigations.summary: Replace direct SQL transport
mitigations.detail: Expose a narrowly scoped catalogue-management API so the spreadsheet sends intended business changes rather than SQL statements.

claims.title: Customer records may be observable between the web API and user database
claims.description: `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` carries customer names, addresses, and payment-card data, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If this internal database connection is not protected, an attacker with a position on the server-side path can intercept those records as `process:web-api` reads or writes `store:user-database`. The capture exposes data that can be used for payment fraud and targeted abuse without querying the application itself.

quotes.text: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` has unstated transport protection and the attacker requires an internal on-path position; impact is high because `store:user-database` is confidential and holds `pii` and `financial` data.

mitigations.summary: Require encrypted database connections
mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` for `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` to TLS and authenticate the database endpoint and web API identity.

mitigations.summary: Limit payment data traversing the connection
mitigations.detail: Tokenize card data and ensure the web API retrieves only the fields needed for each customer operation.

claims.title: Order delivery details may be readable between the web API and SIMS
claims.description: `flow:process:web-api>process:sims>order-handover` sends placed orders including delivery addresses and stored phone numbers, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the server-side handover is unencrypted, an attacker observing that path can intercept customer contact and delivery details before SIMS processes the order. The information then enables targeted social engineering using the dispatch workflow.

quotes.text: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the internal order-handover flow has unstated transport protection and an attacker must reach its path; impact is medium because the flow carries customer delivery and contact information and both endpoints handle `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Protect the API-to-SIMS handover with mTLS
mitigations.detail: Encrypt `flow:process:web-api>process:sims>order-handover` and authenticate both service endpoints with mutually verified identities.

mitigations.summary: Send only dispatch-required fields
mitigations.detail: Avoid including customer contact fields in the handover unless SIMS requires them for fulfillment.

claims.title: Delivery addresses may be readable while SIMS writes the flat file
claims.description: `flow:process:sims>store:delivery-address-flat-file>address-write` carries delivery addresses to `store:delivery-address-flat-file`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the write path is unprotected, an attacker able to observe the SIMS-to-file storage path can intercept addresses as orders are processed. Those addresses can be correlated with order timing and used to target customers outside the application.

quotes.text: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the SIMS-to-file transport protection is unstated and an attacker needs server-side path access; impact is medium because `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is confidential and tagged `pii`.

mitigations.summary: Verify protection of the SIMS storage write path
mitigations.detail: Determine whether `flow:process:sims>store:delivery-address-flat-file>address-write` traverses a networked or local storage path and encrypt any network transport with authenticated TLS.

mitigations.summary: Reduce retained address copies
mitigations.detail: Store only the address fields necessary for dispatch and remove delivery-address files promptly after their operational purpose ends.

claims.title: Dispatch-note PII may be readable between SIMS and the fax gateway
claims.description: `flow:process:sims>process:fax-gateway>dispatch-note` carries a dispatch note with the customer's name and address, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that internal transport is unprotected, an attacker on the path can intercept dispatch PII before `process:fax-gateway` sends the confirmation. The data enables targeted contact with customers using a real order and address.

quotes.text: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because encryption on the SIMS-to-fax-gateway path is unstated and path access is required; impact is medium because the dispatch note carries customer names and addresses handled by PII-tagged processes.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the dispatch-note channel
mitigations.detail: Require mTLS or an equivalently authenticated encrypted transport for `flow:process:sims>process:fax-gateway>dispatch-note`.

mitigations.summary: Minimize dispatch-note contents
mitigations.detail: Use an opaque order reference where the fax gateway can resolve or render only the information required for confirmation.

claims.title: Confirmation faxes may be observable across the customer boundary
claims.description: `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax` crosses from `boundary:sokify-internal-systems` to `boundary:customer-device` and carries the customer's name and address, while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If the fax delivery path lacks confidentiality protection, an attacker positioned on that path can intercept the confirmation and read the PII. The disclosed name-and-address pair can be used to impersonate Sokify in follow-on contact with the customer.

quotes.text: faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the boundary-crossing fax flow's transport protection is unstated and the attacker must observe the delivery path; impact is medium because the confirmation exposes customer names and addresses.

mitigations.summary: Replace fax confirmation with an authenticated encrypted channel
mitigations.detail: Deliver confirmations through a TLS-protected customer channel with recipient authentication rather than `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax`.

mitigations.summary: Limit confirmation content
mitigations.detail: Do not include the full delivery address in customer notifications unless it is necessary for the recipient.

claims.title: Unverified fax destination can disclose confirmations to an unintended recipient
claims.description: An unintended recipient can read the PII in `flow:process:fax-gateway>entity:customer>confirmation-fax` because `process:fax-gateway` sends the confirmation to the stored number without destination verification. The flow crosses into the customer zone and carries the customer's name and address; a stale, misdirected, or attacker-controlled destination number therefore receives the order confirmation. The recipient gains enough personal context to target the customer in later fraud or social-engineering attempts.

quotes.text: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because destination verification is stated absent on the customer-bound fax flow, although the attacker must cause or receive a misdirected fax; impact is medium because the confirmation reveals the customer's name and address.

mitigations.summary: Verify the intended recipient before sending confirmations
mitigations.detail: Require a customer-verified destination identifier and a confirmation mechanism before `process:fax-gateway` releases order details.

mitigations.summary: Use authenticated digital delivery
mitigations.detail: Replace fax with a customer-authenticated portal or verified messaging channel and retain only an opaque confirmation reference in notifications.

claims.title: A copied unencrypted user database would expose customer and card records
claims.description: `store:user-database` is confidential and holds customer names, addresses, and the card they paid with, but `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If this unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker obtaining a database volume, backup, snapshot, or decommissioned copy can read the records directly without authenticating to `process:web-api`. The copied data enables payment fraud and targeted abuse of every customer represented in the database; this is conditional and does not assert that encryption is absent.

quotes.text: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication, or whether the user database and the flat file are encrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because encryption at rest for `store:user-database` is unstated and an attacker needs a storage copy; impact is high because the confidential store holds `pii` and `financial` payment-card data.

mitigations.summary: Establish and enforce encryption at rest for the user database
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:user-database` encryption and require managed-key encryption for its volumes, backups, snapshots, and any replicas or exports.

mitigations.summary: Constrain storage-copy access
mitigations.detail: Restrict backup, snapshot, and restore permissions to separate least-privilege principals and audit all export activity.

claims.title: A copied unencrypted delivery-address file would disclose customer addresses
claims.description: `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is a confidential PII store and its `encryption_at_rest` is unknown. If the flat file is not encrypted at rest, an attacker holding a copied disk, backup, or decommissioned media can read delivery addresses without using SIMS or the normal application access path. The addresses can be combined with dispatch timing to target customers at their homes; this draft is conditional on the unresolved encryption state.

quotes.text: only addresses go in that file, nothing else
Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication, or whether the user database and the flat file are encrypted.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because encryption at rest for `store:delivery-address-flat-file` is unstated and storage-copy access is required; impact is medium because the confidential flat file contains customer delivery addresses.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the delivery-address file and its operational copies
mitigations.detail: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for `store:delivery-address-flat-file`, including backups and migrated or decommissioned media.

mitigations.summary: Reduce flat-file retention and permissions
mitigations.detail: Limit filesystem access to the SIMS identity, delete address files when dispatch processing completes, and prevent untracked copying.

claims.title: Code running in the web API can read customer records through its database access
claims.description: `process:web-api` is internet-facing and uses `flow:process:web-api>store:user-database>customer-records` to keep customer records in `store:user-database`; authentication on that database flow is unknown. An attacker who obtains code execution in `process:web-api` can act through the process's established database access and read customer names, addresses, and payment-card data. The database's at-rest encryption, if present, would not stop this in-component attacker because the application access path decrypts records for authorized use; disclosed cards and addresses enable fraud against affected customers.

quotes.text: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `process:web-api` is internet-facing and both its authentication mechanism and database-flow authentication are unstated, though the attacker must first execute code in it; impact is high because `store:user-database` is confidential and holds `pii` and `financial` data.

mitigations.summary: Scope the web API's database identity to minimum read access
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated least-privilege database identity for `process:web-api`, restrict it to required rows and columns, and separate write-capable operations from ordinary reads.

mitigations.summary: Harden and monitor the web API access path
mitigations.detail: Define the authentication mechanism for `process:web-api`, isolate its runtime identity, and alert on database reads inconsistent with customer requests.
